decisive_items: extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion
response.rationale: R4 best matches the classic complex odontoma presentation: a young patient with a slow-growing calcified maxillary mass, missing molars, and a well-demarcated dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion. R1 (calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor) is the closest alternative but typically has a different calcification pattern and age predilection; the other candidates are too generic, cystic, or lack the missing-tooth association. C1 is a redundant append-only completion of R4 with no independent diagnostic weight.

rejected.why: Generic odontogenic tumor; lacks subtype specificity and does not explain the dense amorphous calcified lesion.
Cemento-ossifying fibroma is well-demarcated but not typically associated with missing teeth or amorphous irregular calcification.
Odontogenic ghost cell tumor can calcify but does not match the dense amorphous lesion with missing molars as well as complex odontoma.
Odontogenic keratocyst is cystic and not densely calcified; does not fit the imaging.
Append-only completion of R4; adds only location already implied by maxillary molar spans, so discounted as a correlated restatement.
